messages:
alex: quick idea — run a lightweight ingest ‘origami skim’ for new quantized models to surface kernel-level tail latency mismatches early. keep it cheap (<=10m), capture per-kernel timelines and a tiny golden trace slice.

maria: can you sketch what the skim does vs our usual smoke/bench?

alex: yeah. smoke = correctness and basic latency. full bench = throughput/cost matrix. skim = focused on p95/p99 jumps caused by kernel fallbacks or unexpected aten->cuda paths. we run a few realistic sequences (2–8 requests, mixed seqlen), log per-op latencies and KV-cache miss heatmap.

alex: example command (prototype):
```bash
./origami-skim --model path/to/artifact --seqlen-samples 8,64,256 --trace-samples 20 --wall-time 600 --out artifacts/skim.json
```

tj: how do we gate on skim results? admit-blocker or advisory?

alex: proposal: advisory by default, auto-fail if p99_growth > 1.5x AND kernel-fallbacks > 3. make it configurable per-model-class. rationale: some models expect p99 spikes at very long seqlen, but unexpected kernel fallbacks are high-signal.

sophie: where do artifacts live and who triages?

alex: artifacts -> s3://redwood-onboard/skim/<model-id>/<run-ts>/skim.json and a small html summary linked to the model intake ticket. triage owned by onboarding oncall first, then runtime team if kernel path looks flaky.

maria: curious about input data — synthetic golden vs prod traces? cost tradeoff.

alex: prefer tiny prod-derived slices (privacy-safe, sampled) + one synthetic golden to validate correctness. prod slices expose real seqlen distribution which helps find kernel mismatch that synthetic often misses.

tj: costwise sounds okay if we cap wall-time, but watch aggregate runs on bursty intake. add quota?

alex: yes, quota + backoff. also suggest sampling policy: only run skim automatically for models flagged as quantized or with new kernel signatures. others opt-in.

bench-bot: automated skim baseline completed for model: gpt-small-quant @ 6723459900 — p99_growth=1.8x, kernel_fallbacks=5, diff-highlight: fused_attention_cuda -> aten_attention_cuda on seqlen=256. report: https://dash.redwood/skim/6723459900

maria: that looks like a real find. can we auto-open a bench-ticket with the diff and attach the skim artifacts?

alex: yep — pipeline will create a ticket with attached skim.json + perf html. triage label: onboard/skim-fail if auto-fail triggered.

sophie: one more ops question — does this need new infra (tracing hooks) or reuse existing bench harness?

alex: minimal new infra: small shim to emit per-kernel breakdown and KV-cache map. reuse bench workers and upload pipeline. target impl: 2 sprint MVP.

tj: :thumbsup: ok let’s pilota few recent model PRs. who wants to own the MVP?

maria: I can take the intake wiring and ticket automation.

sophie: I’ll spec the shim + example outputs.

alex: I’ll wire the sampling policy and thresholds, and run the pilot on the next 5 quantized onboards. bench-bot — please schedule runs during off-peak.

bench-bot: scheduled pilot skim runs for 5 models between 2026-04-01 02:00-06:00 UTC. Artifacts will be uploaded to s3://redwood-onboard/skim/pilot-20260401/

alex: thanks — will post postmortem and tweak thresholds after pilot.

maria: sounds good. thx everyone.
